title: Neon sticks it to A24 by announcing a Creative Commons SCP Foundation movie
summary: Following A24's misstep in pursuing an SCP Foundation film without community input or Creative Commons licensing, Neon announced a competing SCP movie with full CC BY-SA licensing and direct community collaboration.
content:
A24 pissed off one of the internet's largest horror communities when it announced it was working on an SCP Foundation film, but apparently hadn't bothered to contact the SCP Wiki team, nor did it commit to releasing it under a Creative Commons license as required. Seeing an easy PR win, Neon is cashing in by announcing it's making its own SCP movie. But unlike A24, it proactively reached out to the SCP Foundation Wiki team and has pledged to release it under the Creative Commons ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) license.
This is not an "official" SCP film. None of the wiki's staff is involved in the writing or production, it is not receiving compensati …

title: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now
summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon, its next frontier AI model designed for software engineering and cybersecurity, but is limiting initial access to vetted cyber defenders while expanding through government engagement.
content:
Google today revealed its next AI frontier model, which it's calling Gemini 4 Argon. The new model delivers "frontier performance in complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense," according to chief AI architect and Google DeepMind SVP Koray Kavukcuoglu. But the company is limiting access at first to a "set of trusted cyber defenders," and Kavukcuoglu says that Google is "actively engaged in the U.S. government's voluntary process for pre-release model access while we gradually expand access."

title: Samsung gives its two-year-old Galaxy Tab S Plus an overhaul

content:
The Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Ultra arrive together, with no regular Tab S12 in sight. | Image: Samsung	

Since the Galaxy Tab S10 line, Samsung has updated its flagship Ultra tablet annually, but alternates its regular and Plus variants. It means that this year's Galaxy Tab S12 series includes an Ultra model with few changes from last year's Tab S11 Ultra, and a Plus variant that brings a bigger overhaul to the two-year-old Tab S10 Plus. There's no regular Tab S12, suggesting fans of the smaller size will have to wait until 2027 for the next version of that tablet.

Samsung has announced its third-generation Bluetooth tracker, the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It combines a smaller design and improved battery life with a few new tracking and software features, including cross-OS support intended to make it easier to share tracking information with friends and family.
As revealed by leaks, the SmartTag 3 has adopted a squircle design, similar to the original SmartTag but with one key difference: There's no cutout for a key ring. title: Sam Altman says OpenAI won’t go public until its models are safe
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated the company will not pursue an IPO until it can make confident claims about model safety, with no timeline specified. He acknowledged that delaying too long would be harmful, highlighting the tension between ensuring safety and advancing AI progress.
content:
For months, people have wondered when OpenAI will go public. CEO Sam Altman says it won't happen until the company can make better promises about model safety, with no firm timeline in sight. "We intend to continue with AI progress … but as the models have had this surge forward in capability, and we see more of that ahead of us, we have got to be able to make confident safety claims," Altman said Tuesday during a Q&A with reporters after his DevDay keynote. At the same time, he said, waiting too long for an IPO would be "bad for the world."
